safety_boundary: USB-powered continuity mapping of disconnected, de-energized passive assemblies only

footprint_verification.reason: The runner had no installed KiCad footprint path or kicad-cli. Names below are intended KiCad library hints; issue #3 must compare every pad number and land pattern with the cited manufacturer drawing before schematic/PCB freeze.

architecture.controller: Raspberry Pi Pico SC0915, powered and communicating only through its micro-USB connector
architecture.mux_topology: Each bank has low/high groups of eight for independent stimulus and sense paths. All stimulus drain pins share STIM; only one active-high stimulus enable may be asserted. Sense drains for each bank share one ADC input; only one half per bank may be enabled.
architecture.endpoint_network: Connector -> 10 kOhm 1% series resistor -> protected internal node. Internal node has 100 kOhm 1% to BIAS, one BAS70-04 dual-series rail clamp to GND/3V3, one quarter of a TPD4E1U06 to GND, and both stimulus/sense mux channels.
architecture.precheck: With all stimulus enables low, BIAS_CTRL first pulls BIAS low and then becomes high impedance so REF3318 raises BIAS to 1.8 V through 1 kOhm. Every endpoint must follow both phases and ADC_REF must remain in range; missing, saturated, fixed, or inconsistent readings fail closed.
architecture.scan: Complementary high-STIM/low-BIAS and low-STIM/1.8-V-BIAS observations provide an absolute delta test. Firmware must disable STIM, verify all four stimulus-enable shadow bits clear, set STIM, then assert exactly one stimulus enable.
architecture.hardware_default: TMUX1108 EN is active high. External 100 kOhm pulldowns hold all enable nets low while Pico GPIO are unpowered, reset, booting, or high impedance. STIM is also pulled low.

gpio_candidate_map.GP9: STIM (output low/high only after all drive enables read clear)
gpio_candidate_map.GP10: BIAS_CTRL (output low or input/high-Z only; never drive high)
gpio_candidate_map.unused_exposed_gpio: GP14-GP22 remain spare; do not expose raw GPIO through the protocol

components.bom_comments: Use module micro-USB as the only normal power/data input. Do not fit headers when surface mounting. Preserve BOOTSEL and SWD access. ADC pins must be externally clamped and must not be driven while the module is unpowered.

U2/U3 drive A low/high, U4/U5 drive B low/high, U6/U7 sense A low/high, U8/U9 sense B low/high. EN is active high and requires an external pulldown. Fit 100 nF at every VDD pin. VSS and GND both connect to GND for single-supply use.
Provides ADC_REF_1V8 and the high phase of BIAS through R75. Firmware must compare the endpoint high phase to measured ADC_REF; this is diagnostic evidence, not calibration.
Pin 3 is the protected node, pin 1 GND, pin 2 +3V3. Verify this dual-series pin map; do not substitute common-anode/common-cathode variants.
One device per four protected internal endpoint nodes, after the 10 kOhm connector series resistors. Place with a short direct ground return. ESD treatment does not authorize energized testing.
Silkscreen text READY and a distinct ready icon are required; color alone is not status. Verify cathode marking.
Silkscreen text FAULT and a distinct fault icon are required; do not reuse READY's non-color cue. Verify cathode marking.
Exactly one resistor at each connector entry before the protected internal node. Do not bypass on adapters. Standard-mode ratings used: 0.125 W and 150 V.
R33-R64 endpoint node to BIAS; R65-R70 six enable-net pulldowns; R71-R73 address pulldowns; R74 STIM pulldown; R76 START_CANCEL_N pullup. Preserve active-drive EN defaults low.
R75 feeds REF3318 output to BIAS; BIAS_CTRL may pull low or be high-Z only. R77/R78 limit READY/FAULT LED current.
C1-C8 at U2-U9 VDD pins; C9 at REF3318 input. Place directly at supply pins.
REF3318 output/bias reservoir. Confirm latest TI stability guidance during schematic review.
